patch.value: Core per-command help and contracts omit the inherited host flags a core command accepts, so pm contracts --command close lists no --json, --pm-path or --author

Found while fixing pm-gh1666 on 2026.11.7. pm-gh1666 made extension commands publish inherited_flags (owner host, delivered through context.global) in pm contracts --command <cmd> --flags-only --json and inherited_options in pm help <cmd> --json, derived from the reserved host flag table with per-flag extension_command_availability. Core commands still omit them: pm contracts --command close --flags-only --json lists 14 command flags with only --output-format marked inherited, and pm help close --json lists none of --json, --quiet, --pm-path, --author, --no-pager or --expect-hash, although close accepts all of them. An agent that trusts the per-command contract under-uses or re-probes every core command, the same failure GH-1666 reported for extensions. The fix should reuse resolveExtensionCommandInheritedFlagContracts-style data, declare per-command availability of read-output controls (core read surfaces from PM_READ_OUTPUT_SURFACE_CONTRACTS), and keep root-only flags out. Duplicate check: searched inherited host flags, per-command contracts, help options and global flags across all statuses; pm-4bhw (extension help introspection) and pm-xhot (completion from contracts) are closed and do not cover core inherited rows.

pm contracts --command <core-cmd> --flags-only --json carries inherited_flags with owner host for every host flag that command accepts, and excludes read-output controls on commands that are not read surfaces; pm help <core-cmd> --json carries the same rows as inherited_options; A spec invokes every listed inherited flag on a representative read command and a mutating command and none is refused as unknown, with a negative control that drops one row; The contracts fixture and token budgets are updated and stay within their ceilings
Run pm contracts --command close --flags-only --json and pm help close --json, then pm close <id> done --json --pm-path <tracker>
Per-command discovery lists the host flags close accepts, marked host-owned
Neither surface lists --json, --pm-path or --author, although close accepts them

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Scoping measurements (2026-11-07, built CLI 2026.11.7 plus the pm-4of199 tranche), taken before deciding whether this item could join the CLI option-contract batch. It was held out because the help half regresses token cost.

Acceptance on the built CLI: update accepts every reserved host flag except the six read-output controls, which it refuses with "Universal output controls apply only to read commands; update is not a read surface" (code command_failed). get and list accept all of them. --expect-hash parses on every command. So per-command availability is: all reserved host flags, minus read-output controls unless resolveReadOutputSurface(command) is defined, minus any flag the command declares itself (close and list own --author; every core table already carries --output-format as an inherited row).

Cost: pm help close --json is 6,494 bytes today. The extension inherited_options rows (HelpOptionSummary, 12 fields each) cost about 260 bytes per row, so about 16 core rows add about 4.2 KB (+65%) to every per-command help JSON call. pm contracts --command close --flags-only --json rows cost about 110 bytes each, so about +1.8 KB. The multi-command pm contracts --flags-only --json listing is bounded at a 4,500-token default budget and shows 11 of 162 commands. Adding about 16 rows per core command there would push commands out of the default page, so the listing should stay unchanged.

Proposed design: (1) publish inherited_flags only on command-scoped reads (includeSemanticMetadata in buildCommandFlagSurface, src/sdk/cli-contracts/runtime-contracts.ts), derived from RESERVED_EXTENSION_HOST_FLAGS through a shared row builder with resolveExtensionCommandInheritedFlagContracts; (2) for help JSON, either a compact inherited row shape (flags, owner, value_name only) or a pointer to the contracts rows, which needs a ruling because extension commands already emit full rows; (3) the AC spec invokes every listed row on get and update.
